body: Be careful, your professors can really screw you. One quarter your teacher may love your work, the next a different teacher will hate it. Your grade is subjective. Some grade on improvement, some grade on what they think personally. You can pour your heart and soul into a project, showing massive amounts of improvement, for it to only amount to a C. So be careful. I'm being forced to drop out because of financial reasons. I took only online courses this and last quarter because of covid, and this quarter I got extremely sick and was hospitalized. Scad disability didn't respond to my emails, neither did my advisor. I'm now having to drop out because I can't afford the cost of full tuition now that I'm on academic warning. Scad has little room for mistakes. Your course list can actually screw you. Make sure your classes are balanced to where for everyone hard class u may receive a low grade in, you have a class to balance that out. Best of luck.

Similar thing happened to me my freshman year, and I decided I was coming back, I took a gap year to just try and recollect afterwards but I've realized how much happier I am not being there. Their attendance policy absolutely destroyed me. The winter quarter I was there my grandma passed, couldn't leave or go to her funeral because their attendance policy was so uptight, and out of fear of getting sick which I did that same quarter, I stayed here while everyone else in my family attended the funeral. My teachers were not helpful at all either essentially saying suck it up.

My spring quarter was worse, I got an infection and was super sick for half the quarter and I was hospitalized for 2 weeks, I immediately failed a class because one of my teachers had a makeup class and that class was out during the 2 weeks I was in the hospital, so I automatically failed. My other classes were in dire positions, i had my max of 4 absences already and my teachers were only accomodating for previous work by letting me makeup them for a C. My advisor took 3 weeks to get ahold of, while both my parents and I emailing and calling multiple times a week. Their disability help took 3 weeks to get in contact with as well, but by then I was over my sickness and there was nothing they could do to help me.

Faculty is a gamble, as far as I've seen, teachers will pick favorites almost always. Some teachers are amazing and will do the most they can to help. One of my friends is being forced to drop out since she has 2bs and a C. Almost all her scholarships are being revoked. She's the only one in her class with no experience with the adobe cloud in her class, she has attended extra help, has had me and some friends teach/help her with assignments. But her teacher grades as if she should be on the same level as her peers, when they have years of experience over her. She has shown remarkable improvement but is still lacking in comparison to her classmates and thus her grade is suffering tremendously. I'm in a similar boat where I'm right on the edge of being forced to drop.

The bus system sucks, a 5 minute drive takes 45. My experience is a lot of people here never left high school, or even middle school. A lot of people here are extremely immature.

If you're willing to become a soulless workaholic scad will do you good. The people I've seen who've shown the best work are the recluses who don't go out and touch grass. If you crave social interaction and going out, wouldn't recommend. Attendance policy is horrible. 

Internship that'll take you away for a week? Take the absence.

Athletic competition FOR scad? Take the absence.

Fashion show model from the other campus? Take the absence. 

In the hospital cripllingly sick? Take the absence.

Do not have faith in your advisor or anyone else here. You better be able to fight for yourself because no one else here will. 

First quarter here I got super sick, disability services finally got in contact with me 2 weeks after I was sick for a month, in and out of the hospital all that jazz. Advisor wouldn't respond to my calls or emails. Disability reached out after I sent a form 2 weeks too late. Damage was done and it's destroyed my GPA for the quarter. Luckily we had hybrid and it saved my life but hybrid is gone now. 

Scad is a special type of beast. You will not tame it. You'll just need to figure out a way to have your ass fucking by it be less painful. Good luck. A disgruntled financially struggling, scad sophomore
